text.p: Two goals in the last three minutes sent Benfica spinning to a remarkable 4-3 home defeat by Salgueiros in the Portuguese league on Sunday.
The defeat left the Lisbon side seven points behind second placed Sporting who beat titleholders and league leaders Porto 2-1 away on Saturday.

Without some spectacular saves from Belgian keeper Michel Preud'homme, Benfica's chaotic defence might have suffered even greater ignominy ahead of their Cup Winners' Cup quarter-final second leg against Fiorentina in Italy on Thursday.

They opened the scoring in the 15th minute when winger Edgar Pacheco knocked in a neat pass from captain Joao Pinto, but Salgueiros made a series of bold counter-attacks which frequently embarrased their opponents.
They equalised in the 36th minute with a shot from midfielder Abilio Novais and went ahead in the 63rd with a goal by striker Fernando Nandinho.
One minute later Benfica equalised again after Moroccan Tahar Kalej rescued the ball from a goalmouth scramble and they went 3-2 ahead 10 minutes from the end through Joao Pinto.
It did not last. Two defensive errors in the closing minutes allowed unmarked Brazilian substitute Marcos Severo to score in the 89th minute and again in injury time to clinch an unlikely victory.
Benfica coach Manuel Jose attributed his team's defeat to a "loss of calm and confidence."
Porto's defeat against Sporting was the first time the titleholders had lost at home to their Lisbon rivals in 21 years.
Porto now meet Manchester United in Oporto in the quarter finals of the European Cup on Wednesday with morale still delicate after their crushing 4-0 defeat in England in the first leg.
